CT561 Paper-Based Topic Guide

Stock-and-Flow Modelling from Text

The recurring exam task is to convert a scenario into stocks, material flows, auxiliaries, equations, units and signed information links.

Recent-paper question forms

  • One-stock workload model [10-12]: identify the backlog, its inflows/outflows and all stated pressure-response links.
  • Two-stock university/workforce model [8-15]: Students and Staff, ratios, desired staff, attrition and hires.
  • Resource-constrained transition [12]: a flow cannot exceed demand, available resource or operational capacity.
  • Equation-to-model [8]: convert a differential equation into stock, flows, feedbacks and units.

References: 2023/24 Q1(b), 2024/25 Q1(b), 2025/26 Q3(b), 2021/22 Q1(b), Q2(a,b), and 2016/17 Q2(a,b).

Construction order in the exam

  1. Circle quantities that exist at a time. These are stocks.
  2. Underline quantities measured per time. These are flows.
  3. Draw each stock as a rectangle, then add only the material inflows/outflows named in the question.
  4. Add auxiliaries and information arrows. Give every arrow a sign if requested.
  5. Write stock equations first. Add flow equations only when asked.
  6. Check units: people/day x day = people.

Core equations and diagram rules

Stock = INTEG(total inflow - total outflow, initial stock)
Fractional inflow = stock x fraction/time
Fractional outflow = stock x fraction/time
Adjustment flow = (desired stock - actual stock)/adjustment time
  • A stock is an accumulation, such as Claims Backlog, Staff or Susceptible People.
  • A flow changes the stock, such as Claims Completed, Hires, Recoveries or Vaccinations.
  • An auxiliary changes a flow but does not itself accumulate, such as Work Pressure, Desired Staff or Average Productivity.
  • Clouds are optional unless your lecturer requires them. The stock, pipes, flow names, auxiliaries and information arrows are essential.

Paper-derived model: resource-constrained vaccination [12]

2021/22 Q2(b) requires Unvaccinated People to move to Vaccinated People, limited by people waiting, vaccine stock and medic capacity.

Total Daily Capacity = Number of Medics x Average Productivity
Vaccines Dispensed = MIN(Unvaccinated People, Number of Vaccines, Total Daily Capacity)
Unvaccinated = INTEG(-Vaccines Dispensed, U0)
Vaccinated = INTEG(Vaccines Dispensed, 0)
Number of Vaccines = INTEG(-Vaccines Dispensed + Deliveries, V0)

For 10,000 unvaccinated people, 100 medics, 20 vaccines/medic/day and 10,000 vaccines: capacity is 2,000/day, so the flow is 2,000/day. If vaccines are zero, the flow is zero even if medics are available.

Equation-to-stock-flow route

For the 2021/22 population equation dP/dt = rP(1-P/C) - sP, write:

Population = INTEG(Births - Decline, P0)
Births = r x Population x (1 - Population/Carrying Capacity)
Decline = s x Population

The carrying-capacity term is a balancing feedback. Population reaches C only when decline is zero and the logistic inflow becomes zero at C. Give units for every variable.

Mark checklist

  • Every stock has an initial value or named initial condition.
  • Every material flow changes exactly the correct stock(s).
  • Ratios put the stated numerator above the stated denominator.
  • Use MIN when a paper gives multiple binding physical constraints.
  • Do not invent extra causal links or equations not supported by the scenario.
